_enabled: The operator enables the experiment. Unless this is the JSON value true, every mr-tester-ab command prints AB-SKIP disabled and mr-spawn renders the brief without the experiment's sentence.
_cache_root: Shadow testers write their tests under cache_root, outside the game repo; a shadow that names the builder's worktree instead is marked contaminated by `collect`, which lists the paths to remove. Replays run in <cache_root>/scratch, and each judge bundle gets a directory of its own under <cache_root>/judge.
_eligibility: A slice is in the experiment when it is listed in required_slices or starts with a prefix, is not in exclude_slices, and has a tester call. A slice has none when its type is in no_tester_types: the `type:` its launch vars carry, or the `type:` line of its section in a spec under specs_dir of harness_repo. A slice with no tester whose section states no type (a study such as np-b, a doc-only slice) is listed in exclude_slices.
_reserve: USD by model. The cap counts every planned arm at its reserve until its run has a price: a slice planned and not collected, a shadow that failed, a transcript that could not be priced. Each is about twice the dearest run of that model measured on two slices (sonnet 1.72, opus 4.34); five arms reserve 16 against a measured 10.34 for five runs.
_collect: `collect` prints AB-WAIT and records nothing while a shadow has a transcript that does not end in a final message and whose export holds no output file. A transcript silent for shadow_stalled_s is a run that died: it no longer holds the collect.
_escapes: With escapes_in_session, `escapes` replays the shadow suites at the snapshot it records and hands the builder up to handoff_limit failing tests with the adoption rule; false makes it record the snapshot only, and failing shadow tests are then judged at the close. Five suites replay at one snapshot in 10-110 s (client, or Rust with a warm target directory); a cold Rust build or a first wasm build runs past escapes_budget_s: `escapes` then says so, writes no result for a suite it stopped or did not reach, and `score` replays those at merge. The budget stays under 120 s: `escapes` runs in the builder's foreground Bash call, which the Bash tool stops at that default.
_port: No pass rewrites a shadow test so that it compiles: every runnable shadow test file compiled at the first green snapshot on the two measured slices. A file that does not compile is charged to its arm.
_close: `finalize`, and `close-check` on the audit of any slice the experiment did not plan, close the experiment when every slice in required_slices is finalized and merged with no planned slice left unfinalized, when max_scored_slices slices are scored, when the cap is reached, or when the default branch has commits on loop_active_days distinct days since the first finalized slice. With required_slices empty the first condition is off and the other three close it; `status` prints where each stands. The days backstop is met by days passing after the last eligible slice has merged, which is why every audit asks.
_test_patterns: `test` finds a test and captures its name: in Rust a test attribute, then any further attributes and `//` comment lines (a criterion tag may sit under `#[test]`), then the `fn`. `body` is the bracket that opens the test's body, so the tool knows where a test ends and can tell the tests an arm wrote (new, or changed against the base tree) from those already in a file it edited: only the arm's own are run, counted and priced.
_runners: Each arm's test files are overlaid on a snapshot in <cache_root>/scratch and run by the first runner whose match fits. {files} expands to the files, {packages} to a -p pair per cargo package they belong to, {names} to their test names as a regex alternation, {scope} to the runner's `scopes` expression of each file joined by ` | ` ({stem} is the file's name without its extension: an integration test is its own binary, any other Rust test file is a module), {junit} to the report path, {tool} to this directory. `junit` names a report the runner writes itself, relative to the scratch directory: nextest writes under the workspace's own target/ whatever CARGO_TARGET_DIR says. `probe` must exit 0 before the runner is used. Each `setup` step runs when its `if_missing` path (relative to `cwd`) is absent or when the snapshot's `stamp` paths (relative to the tree) differ from those it last ran against: installed packages follow the lockfile of the snapshot being replayed, and the wasm package the client's tests import is rebuilt when its sources change. A step that fails stops the score unless it is `optional`; after an optional step failed, a test or a test file whose failure text matches `unresolved` (an import that does not resolve) is recorded not-run with that reason, never as a failure of the test. With every step done, a file the runner reports as failed while reporting none of its tests (it does not parse, or statically imports a module that does not exist) is no-compile, a false positive of its arm, as a Rust file that does not build. `no_tests_rc` is the exit code of the runner when the build held none of the tests asked for (a Rust file no `mod` line names): those tests are not-run, not no-compile. A file no runner fits (Playwright specs) is recorded not-run.
_runner_env: Every replay and seeded-defect command runs with runner_env set (a quarter of this machine's 32 cores: other slices build and run time-bounded gates beside it) and with the runner_path directories that exist ahead of PATH (the game's pinned toolchain: the caller's PATH may resolve another node).
_mutants: The seeded-defect measure, reported beside confirmed findings and never a gate: on a slice whose merged diff changes a matching file, the changed lines are mutated once per arm with only the tests that arm wrote and that pass at merge deciding what is caught: `runner` names the runner whose scopes keep the run to the arm's own files, so a test of the same name in the gating suite kills nothing for the arm. One wall budget covers the slice: about 8 s a mutant and arm, so five arms stay inside it up to roughly 80 mutants, and an arm it does not reach is recorded `budget`. `ok_rc` lists the exit codes that leave usable result lists (cargo-mutants: 0 all caught, 2 some missed, 3 some timed out); any other, such as 4 for a baseline that fails, is recorded `error`.
_areas: The area of a slice is the one pattern its merged diff matches, mixed when it matches both, other when neither.
_prices: USD, measured 24 Oct - 12 Nov 2026 unless noted. lens_caught: mean in-session fix cycle after a lens batch (8.74, n=27) less the median closeout baseline (0.95, n=44); lens_caught_low: the median fix cycle (6.30) less the same baseline. post_merge: median ci-fix slice (n=9), the price of an escape, base or spec miss in the central scenario. escape_high: median residual-fix slice, Aug-Oct ledger (n=91, cost columns unreliable). spec_high: median relaunched slice after a park (n=18). fp: mean post-lens tester re-invocation (n=29), also the price of a brittle break; fp_low: its median. flake: median ci-fix slice. Scenarios: low prices every miss at lens_caught_low and a false positive at fp_low; central prices a lens-caught miss at lens_caught and any other at post_merge; high prices escape and base misses at escape_high and spec misses at spec_high.
_bloat: What a test line costs later sessions: tokens_per_line tokens, read fresh fresh_reads times and carried in a cache for cached_turns turns. Measured over 20 build sessions with a tester: 11-13 tokens a line, a mean of 5 reads of a tester's files by another context and 18 turns after the first such read. About $0.0003 a line.
